scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Sadi Moma originated in Bulgaria as a traditional folk song and associated folk dance.
The title translates to 'A Girl Plants', referring to the opening lyrics of the narrative folk song.
Over time, the tune became a recognized piece of Bulgarian heritage and notably crossed into modern culture when Richard Stallman adapted its melody for the Free Software Song.

Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The song's narrative reflects village life, agriculture, and folk humor, detailing the regret and reward of agricultural work (planting vines) followed by a cautionary tale of a soldier's binge drinking.
It serves as social folk recreation in line and circle formations.
Today it is a living tradition.
